query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a minor amount of Sn to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys can increase the coercivity by promoting the formation of BCC phases and phase boundary regions, which can lead to a higher volume fraction of BCC phase and a decrease in the volume fraction of FCC phase.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with a mixed structure of FCC and BCC phases
generation.intervention: Addition of a minor amount of Sn
generation.conditions: The alloy should have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of BCC phases and phase boundary regions
generation.mechanism: The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phases and phase boundary regions, leading to an increase in coercivity
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercivity compared to the prior derivatives
generation.baseline: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys without Sn addition
generation.boundary: The alloy should have a composition that meets the high-entropy alloy criteria
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Sn required to achieve the desired coercivity and the potential effects of other elements on the alloy's properties

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with and without Sn addition, and measure their coercivity using a vibrating sample magnetometer or a hysteresis curve test system
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Sn does not lead to an increase in coercivity, the hypothesis is falsified

In our previous work [], the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA consisting of BCC and FCC phases shows good magnetic and mechanical properties, and it was found that BCC phases show a higher Ms than that of FCC phases for the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The other work of our group [] found a minor amount of Ga addition into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA can promote the formation of BCC phase and improve the Ms of the alloy, and the value of remanence (Br) and coercivity (Hc) also increases. It was reported that the addition of Sn can hinder the formation of FCC phase [] and promote the formation of BCC phase []. Therefore, in this work, a minor amount of Sn was added into the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA hoping to get a higher volume fraction of BCC phase.
In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were studied from phase constitutions to microst

ometer (STEM/EDS, JEM-2100F, JEOL, Ltd., Tokyo, Japan). The Ms and thermomagnetic curves was obtained from vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM, Lakeshore 7407, Westerville, OH, USA). The coercivity (Hc), hysteresis losses (Pu), remanence (Br), initial permeability (μi), and maximum permeability (μmax) were obtained from hysteresis curves (DC) test system (HCTS, FE-2100SD, Forever elegance, Hunan, China) using a 27 × 9 × 1.7 mm rectangular sample at a magnetic field of 25 kA/m. The thermal stability was analyzed by differential scanning calorimeter (DSC, DIAMOND) at a heating rate of 10 K/min.
## 3.1. X-ray Diffraction
Figure 1 shows the XRD patterns of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. It is found that all of these HEAs consist of a mixed structure of FCC phase and BCC phase. A few diffraction peaks of unknown phases appear in the XRD patterns for x ≥ 0.02 and it is especially obvious for x ≥ 0.06. Here, I(111)FCC and I(110)BCC were used to denote the diffraction intensity of the strongest peak of (111) for FCC phase and (110) for BCC phase, respectively. It is obvious that the Ms, coercivity (Hc), and hysteresis losses (Pu) increase while the initial permeability (μi) and maximum permeability (μmax) have a generally decreasing trend with increasing x. These results may be due to the increase of the volume fraction of BCC phase and the decrease of the volume fraction of FCC phase, which is in agreement with that of reported FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Gax (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.08) HEAs [].
